title: U.S. House · New York's 20th Congressional District
area: Capital Region, covering Albany, Schenectady, and Amsterdam and surrounding areas.

context.text: Both parties' primaries were canceled: incumbent Paul Tonko advanced unopposed on the Democratic and Working Families Party lines, and Ralph Ambrosio advanced unopposed on the Republican and Conservative Party lines. As of September 22, 2026, Cook Political Report and Inside Elections rated the general election "Solid Democratic" and Decision Desk and Sabato's Crystal Ball rated it "Safe Democratic."

summary.text: Paul Tonko is the incumbent U.S. Representative for New York's 20th Congressional District, first elected in 2008. A former engineer and longtime state legislator, he sits on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and the House Budget Committee.

background.text: Born in Amsterdam, New York in 1949; earned a bachelor's degree in industrial and mechanical engineering from Clarkson University in 1971; worked as a public works engineer and state transportation agency employee.

Served on the Montgomery County Board of Supervisors (1976-1983, chairman in 1981) and in the New York State Assembly (1983-2007); served as president of the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) from 2007 to 2008.

record.text: Serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee (Oversight and Investigations; Energy; Environment subcommittees) and the House Budget Committee in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Chaired the House Energy and Commerce Committee's Environment and Climate Change Subcommittee in the 117th Congress (2021-2022).

summary.text: Ralph Ambrosio is the Republican and Conservative Party nominee for NY-20, having advanced unopposed after both primaries were canceled. He has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and Ballotpedia's profile of him contains no independent biography.

researchNotes: This race is rated Solid/Safe Democratic. Ambrosio has almost no public footprint: no completed Ballotpedia survey and no biography section on his Ballotpedia page, so his entry is marked minimal. Tonko has not stated specific 2026 campaign priorities on his Ballotpedia page; his entry here relies on biography and committee assignments.
